variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A circuit breaker is a stateful policy around a remote call. It observes recent outcomes, temporarily blocks calls when failure or slowness crosses a boundary, and admits a limited set of probes before restoring normal traffic.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Closed
pairs.detail: Calls reach the dependency while the breaker records failures, timeouts, and slow responses in a bounded window.
pairs.explanation: Calls reach the dependency while the breaker records failures, timeouts, and slow responses in a bounded window.

pairs.label: Open
pairs.detail: Calls do not reach the unhealthy dependency.
pairs.explanation: Calls do not reach the unhealthy dependency. The caller returns a controlled error or an explicitly designed degraded response.

pairs.label: Half-open
pairs.detail: Only a small number of representative calls pass.
pairs.explanation: Only a small number of representative calls pass. Their outcomes decide whether normal traffic returns or the circuit opens again.

variants.hint:
Closed: Calls reach the dependency while the breaker records failures, timeouts, and slow responses in a bounded window.

Open: Calls do not reach the unhealthy dependency.

Half-open: Only a small number of representative calls pass.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Bound one attempt
pairs.detail: Stop waiting before the caller's end-to-end latency budget is exhausted.
pairs.explanation: Stop waiting before the caller's end-to-end latency budget is exhausted.

pairs.label: Retry only transient faults
pairs.detail: Use a small attempt limit, backoff, jitter, idempotency, and one aggregate retry budget.
pairs.explanation: Use a small attempt limit, backoff, jitter, idempotency, and one aggregate retry budget.

pairs.label: Stop repeated doomed calls
pairs.detail: Open after enough recent evidence and make retry logic stop when the breaker rejects.

pairs.label: Reserve independent capacity

variants.prompt: Why should independent shards or regions usually have separate breakers?
options: One global breaker can block healthy paths because an unrelated failure is aggregated into it
Separate breakers make every operation idempotent
A breaker must run inside the dependency
Regions never share failure modes
variants.explanation: Breaker scope should match the failure domain. Aggregating independent resources can turn a local failure into unnecessary global rejection.
